title: STEGO
description: STEGO generates service and client code from one declaration and a registry of trusted components. Platform engineers write the components. Service authors and agents write the declaration and the fills. The same declaration and the same registry always produce the same code. Every service built from one archetype has the same shape, so a reviewer who can read one can read any other. STEGO refuses invalid input before it writes a file, and it recovers an interrupted write. Generation is the only way generated code changes, so a fix is a version bump and a new run, and every change is a diff a reviewer can read. STEGO can also name every service built from a component, tell a consumer when that component is superseded, qualify its own releases, and record the evidence for each requirement it claims to meet.
notes: Recorded decisions, 2026-10-27. The core promises are determinism, uniformity, and refusal before damage. Independent output is not a promise. A pinned STEGO library is allowed for security primitives such as token verification, session encryption and TLS checks, while the service's own shape and logic carry no STEGO dependency. A fix reaches a service as a version bump and a new generation run, never as a hand edit, because a regenerated diff is auditable and a hand edit is not. Apply reports every hand-edited generated file and refuses to write unless the run is told it may replace them. The record of what a service was built from extends .stego/state.yaml rather than sitting in a second file, because that file already exists wherever STEGO is used; it needs a service name, real per-component digests, and a stated format contract. One signed compiler holds every generator: separately releasable generators were rejected, because they would rebuild the trust model once per generator, and Go has no safe dynamic plugin path. Patch latency comes instead from pinning the compiler and the registry independently and from real per-component digests. See ST-STD-TRUST.
